generatedCommentsNodes.comment: There is a unit mismatch when assigning `maxTaskProcessingQuantumMs` to `this.maxTaskProcessingQuantumNs`. The parameter is provided in milliseconds, but it is assigned directly to a field intended to hold nanoseconds without conversion. This results in the quantum being significantly smaller than intended (e.g., 1000ns instead of 1,000,000,000ns) when a custom value is specified. It should be converted using `TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos()`.

review_comment:
Yeah, in CFS this should be the target latency within a process should get its guaranteed fair schedule/chance to run IIRC.
And here, have a similarish meaning i.e. I/O will get its chance to run after this, although with a delay (our tasks are not preemptive).

TBH what CFS does is to update via a timer (the OS tick rate) the virtual time of the task running on CPU, guaranteed a min granularity time to run on the CPU or eventually perform a different decision if there are more.
